#3370. 10 Hacks Every Reddit User Should Know

If you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit. From mainstream sports to niche crafts, it does seem that there's some kind of Reddit community for everyone. (And if there's not one, you can make one yourself.) If you're using Reddit, here are 10 hacks you should know about to improve your experience on the site.

Reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private. You can hide your posts, comments, and the subreddits you're a part of. If you want to do this, click your profile icon once you've logged in to Reddit, and go to Settings > Profile. Alternatively, you can follow the direct link to Reddit's profile settings page. Click the drop-down menu next to Content & Activity, and select Hide all. You should also turn off Online Status on the same page to stop people from seeing when you're using Reddit.

Old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI. Old Reddit looks dated, but it doesn't have infinite scrolling, distracting animations, and a bunch of features designed to increase the time you spend on the platform. It's no wonder that Reddit is making it harder to access this version of the site. As long as it's around, you should switch to Old Reddit for a cleaner reading experience. You can do that by going to Reddit Settings > Preferences and enabling Default to Old Reddit. You can also visit old.reddit.com, though you'll need to sign in for access

Many subreddits use custom themes that range from beautiful to borderline unusable. If you want a more consistent UI across the site, you should disable these custom subreddit styles. Go to Reddit Settings > Preferences and turn off Use community themes. If you're using Old Reddit, click the preferences button in the top-right corner, and under "display options," disable allow subreddits to show me custom themes.

A multireddit is a feed that shows posts from a customized group of subreddits. You can think of it as a way to break out of Reddit's algorithms, and create your own Reddit feed. I use multireddits to follow all sports-related subs I'm interested in. I even have one for gaming, and one for fountain pens. It's a great way to create interest-specific feeds, and if you make them private, no one else can see them. To create one, click the Create custom feed button in the left pane in new Reddit. In the Old Reddit design, click the Create button in the left pane. Be sure to select the Private button to keep it from showing up for others. You can add as many subreddits as you like to the list, and bookmark the feed to access it whenever you wish to.

Reddit has recently adopted an Instagram-like experience for its feeds. It removed the ability to sort posts by new, controversial, best, etc., and instead offers "For You" and "Following." If you dislike this change, you can bypass it. I use Reddit on mobile Safari, and I recommend an extension called Sink It for Reddit. It can automatically redirect you to Old Reddit, and there's a feature that optimizes it for mobile, which brings back the old sorting options. You can also use third-party apps such as RedReader for Android, or RDX for Reddit on an iPhone or iPad to restore the old sorting options for Reddit posts.

After all these years, Reddit's built-in search still leaves something to be desired—at least, on the surface. To find posts on Reddit faster, use search filters on the site. For instance, adding "title:" to your search will limit the results to post titles, and boolean operators such as AND, OR, and NOT also work for advanced searches on the site.

#3369. Stephen King Praises Hit 4-Part Thriller As "The Best Cop Show On TV"

Stephen King just revealed what he considers to be the best police procedural on TV.

The bestselling horror author is known for publishing such hits as Carrie, The Shining, The Stand, The Dark Tower, Pet Sematary, It, Misery ,and The Green Mile. When he's not writing, King takes to social media to share his views on current events and gives recommendations for the books, TV shows, and movies he believes his fans should consume.

On that latter front, he has done it again. On X, King showered praise on the British series Blue Lights, calling it "the best cop show on TV," and singled out the season 1 episode "Full Moon Fever," which he believes "deserves all the kudos there are." He also acknowledged that a reviewer once compared Blue Lights to The Pitt due to the authentic way it depicts the field of law enforcement, similar to how The Pitt does the same for medicine.

"BLUE LIGHTS (Britbox): The best cop show on TV, and one episode 'Full Moon Fever'--deserves all the kudos there are. Some critic said 'It's THE PITT with police.' Smart critic."

Blue Lights premiered in 2023 and centers on three recruits—Grace, Annie and Tommy—who work for the Police Service of Northern Ireland at Blackthorn Station as they deal with gangs, feuds, and division in the city.

Sian Brooke, Katherine Devlin, Nathan Braniff, Martin McCann, Richard Dormer, Hannah McClean, Andi Osho, Jonathan Harden, and John Lynch star in the series, which was created by Declan Lawn and Adam Patterson.

With a critics' score of 91% and an audience score of 87% on Rotten Tomatoes, Blue Lights has earned positive reviews throughout its run on the air and won Best Drama Series at the BAFTA TV Awards last year.

Blue Lights is available to stream on BritBox and ended its fourth season earlier this month. While BBC One has not renewed Blue Lights for season 5 yet, if it were to come back, Lawn and Patterson won't be there as they recently revealed they've exited the production to work on other projects.

King is no stranger to the world of television, as many of his novels have been adapted for the small screen over the years, including It, 11.22.63, The Mist, Mr. Mercedes, The Outsider, The Stand, Chapelwaite, and The Institute.

His very first book, Carrie, was recently given the TV treatment on Prime Video, courtesy of Mike Flanagan, who previously adapted King's Gerald's Game, Doctor Sleep, and The Life of Chuck.

With Summer H. Howell in the title role, Carrie received positive reviews this fall from critics and audiences alike, and King, who serves as an executive producer, gave it his stamp of approval.

Adaptations of King's books have been hit or miss, according to the author himself. He hasn't been shy about expressing when a film or show hasn't met his expectations. On the flip side, he's always eager to share his recommendations from other creators and storytellers, like he has done with Blue Lights.

As viewers wait to find out whether the series gets renewed, perhaps Stephen King's positive reception will create new fans and help the network with its decision.

Blue Lights (2023) is a police drama set in Belfast, following three new PSNI recruits as they learn how dangerous and complicated frontline policing can be. Their training quickly becomes a test of judgment and survival as they face criminal gangs, divided communities, and the pressures that come with policing a city still shaped by its troubled past.

#3368. A24’s TV Division Is Quietly Having as Strong a Year as Its Film Team

Maybe it’s just because we can’t get enough headlines and discussion about “Backrooms” and “You Can See Everything,” but despite the banner year A24 has had at the box office, its TV division has quietly had nearly as strong of a year.

The indie label has produced more shows in 2026 than in any year in its history, including sleeper commercial and critical hits across the board, and even managed to land shows on virtually every streamer in town.

Led by Sam French, the U.S. head of TV at A24, the studio this year has cranked out the third season of “Euphoria” on HBO Max, the second season of “Beef” and the third season of “Survival of the Thickest” both on Netflix, “Margo’s Got Money Troubles” on Apple TV, the “Friday the 13th” prequel series “Crystal Lake” on Peacock, and most recently the British sitcom “It Gets Worse” on Paramount+ led by the UK Heads Piers Wenger and Rose Garnett. Its unscripted division, led by Johnny Hausfater, has also ramped up aggressively, with shows like “Neighbors,” “Born to Bowl,” and “Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow” all on HBO Max. Related Stories Sean Connery Wasn’t the First James Bond: Meet Barry Nelson in the ‘Casino Royale’ You’ve Never Seen ‘The Other Bennet Sister’ Christmas Special Trailer: Can Mary Bennet Still Be Herself and ‘the Perfect Wife’?

Not unlike its film slate, its series have been a blend of auteur-driven prestige and genre shows with a twist. The David E. Kelley series “Margo’s Got Money Troubles” is a tongue-in-cheek, real-world satire on motherhood and the modern economy about a young single mom played by Elle Fanning who needs to turn to OnlyFans for extra cash. On the other side of the coin, “Crystal Lake” follows masked killer Jason Voorhees’ mom and stands out from other modern horror TV shows by, as our critic wrote, not trying to secretly be a family drama or a slapstick comedy or some other genre or metaphor, but it just amplifies the grisly kills in the best way it can.

The recurring theme between these shows isn’t genre but the stamp of quality that A24 lends.

While something like “Beef” saw a steep drop in viewership of a reported 60 percent between its first and second seasons, “Euphoria” in its return was up 17 percent in its finale ratings compared to Season 2. “Crystal Lake” was also a big hit on Peacock, its top show on the streamer last month, logging 1.3 billion minutes watched over its first 11 days, making it the fourth-highest scripted original series ever on Peacock. A24 now has roughly 30 to 40 shows in various stages of development, pre-production, or active production, with its executive team expanding from about 15 from just 3 people in its early days.

It’s been able to ramp up firstly because of its partnership with numerous TV buyers across the major streamers, but also because of working with largely first-time creators and showrunners. While “Crystal Lake” is a notable exception, A24 generally is operating on its TV side the same way it does with its film, leading with the artist and the project they want to pursue rather than the IP.

That has produced some very personal and idiosyncratic projects over the years like “Ramy” and “The Curse,” the latter of which was the kernel of getting Nathan Fielder to working with A24 again on “You Can See Everything.”

The breadth of content A24 has amassed on its TV side and continually making shows that have the same barrier-pushing flavor and stamp of quality that has become known with A24’s brand is what will help make it as essential a part of the company’s overall business and valuation as its film and distribution business. But we’re seeing even its TV division branching out and embracing IP and tentpoles in the same way its film side has.

Coming up for A24 are a Claire Danes and Ewan McGregor drama “The Spot” on Hulu and “The Apology” with Gwyneth Paltrow on Netflix, which already got a two-season order and was an example of a show that grew out of Paltrow being convinced to try TV after already working with A24 on the film side for “Marty Supreme.” The studio is also is working with Ben Stiller on a New York Knicks documentary series for HBO and a competition cooking show based on the video game “Overcooked” for Netflix. A24 could’ve made a Knicks series with anyone, but teaming with a superfan like Stiller was another example of putting the creator above the concept.

Yet, both a strength and weakness of its TV model is that it does not have a distribution mechanism the way it does on the film side. It’s not bogged down with an unprofitable streamer, a dwindling linear cable channel, or a broadcast network, but that makes it reliant on the many partners it has built up across the industry.

Warner Bros. merging with Paramount arguably reduces the buyers in the market, even if there are still two streamers at Skydance. Netflix just had a massive shakeup of its leadership team that could easily have a different attitude toward A24’s series. And the overall industry trends around the end of Peak TV mean it’s always a volatile business for independents in the TV space.

But no one saw “Backrooms” or “You Can See Everything” coming either, and A24 has as good a chance as any to have lightning strike twice with the next “Euphoria” or “Beef.”

Hannah covers horror, sci-fi, and games at Collider, where she writes news and features, reviews new releases, and interviews the people who make them. She’s helping build out Collider’s gaming coverage, with Pokémon as one of her specialties. If she isn’t writing about a monster, she’s probably watching one on a tape from her VHS collection.

Geralt of Rivia made up the “of Rivia” part because he thought it would get him more work. Four seasons into The Witcher, a queen finally makes the name official, and the person who’d appreciate that story most is Ciri. Back at Kaer Morhen, Geralt had already once let her in on a secret that’s a little embarrassing for a man who makes his living killing monsters: when he was a boy, he wanted to be a knight. By the time he gets his wish, he’d trade it for an afternoon with his daughter.

It’s been more than a year since Liam Hemsworth took over for Henry Cavill, and one of the stranger consequences of the timing is how little of his run he’s gotten to spend with Freya Allan, because Geralt and Ciri were already separated when Hemsworth picked up the sword. With Netflix filming the final two seasons back-to-back, the expectation was that viewers who saw his first season in October 2025 would get the rest of that story this year.

Netflix has officially slated The Witcher Season 5 onto its release schedule for 2027 or later. In its November 16 announcement from the Texas Book Festival, the streamer listed Geralt’s final outing among the book adaptations coming in “2027 and beyond,” alongside Bridgerton Season 5 and Narnia: The Magician's Nephew. Netflix has yet to announce an exact premiere date for The Witcher's fifth and final season.

Four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

You want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

You would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

Geralt has spent the better part of a season looking for Ciri, and even if somebody handed him a map with her whereabouts marked on it, he’d still be working with bad information. The girl he remembers training at Kaer Morhen has fallen in love, found a home with the Rats, and watched Leo Bonhart (Sharlto Copley) murder every last one of them, ending with Bonhart taking Ciri alive. Whatever Geralt imagines he’ll need to do for his daughter when he finds her, he has no idea yet what happened to Mistle or what Ciri had to see.

Then there’s Ciri’s biological father, who has come to an ugly conclusion about the man who raised her. Emhyr (Bart Edwards) once owed Geralt his life. By the end of Season 4, his advisers have convinced him that the bond between Geralt and Ciri is the reason he keeps failing to find his daughter. The emperor closes the season by walking up to a cell and giving the creature behind the bars Geralt’s name. After four seasons of people hunting Ciri for what her blood can do, someone has finally figured out what makes her father vulnerable. Everybody on the Continent knows who he’ll come for.

The first four seasons of The Witcher are streaming on Netflix. Stay tuned with Collider for future updates on the release of Season 5.

#3366. 10 Hacks Every Hulu User Should Know

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

If you don't like the content Hulu is suggesting for you, you have several options to curate your recommendations. "Disliking" a show or movie removes it from your Home view and You May Also Like entirely, so the only way you'll see that content is if you search for it. You can dislike on the Details page if you're watching on your TV or use the thumbs down on mobile or web. (The "Like" button will obviously influence your algorithm in the opposite way). If your "Continue Watching" queue is cluttered with shows you started but didn't like enough to finish, you can remove them from your watch history as well as the My Stuff list. This, too, will allow content to remain searchable but not suggested in other areas of the app.

If PIN protection is enabled, users must enter a four-digit PIN when switching between profiles on a single account. This is intended as a parental control feature, since it's available on non-Kids profiles and can keep children from accessing more mature content on an adult's profile. However, you can also enable this feature to keep other users from seeing your viewing history and preferences or influencing your algorithm by watching their content under your profile (accidentally or on purpose). To set up a PIN, log into your account on Hulu's website, select your profile, and go to Manage Profiles > Parental Controls. You'll have to choose a PIN and enter your password to confirm the changes.

Another approach to protecting your profile and algorithm is to set up separate profiles for specific use cases, such as when you have guests or if you host watch parties for certain shows. This keeps content from influencing your recommendations and prevents other viewers from seeing what's in your watch history or saved content (especially if there are things you want to keep private).

If you find that subtitles and captions are too bold—or not visible enough—you can change the font, color, size, and style from the default so they enhance your viewing experience rather than detracting from it. Hulu allows you to adjust the color and opacity of the font, background, and window so you get the right contrast, and you can also select the specific font and font scaling. On your streaming device, go to Settings > Subtitles & Captions, then hit the back button on your remote to save your preferences. You can update these settings on mobile and desktop as well.

If you have a long list of shows and films to watch but can't decide what to start next, look for the "Expiring Soon" badge to see which titles are leaving the service in the next two weeks. Badges display the number of days remaining, so you can determine what to prioritize and whether it's worth diving in based on how much time you have to finish before the expiration date. Go to "My Stuff" to monitor saved titles that are expiring soon.

If you've been watching Hulu under an account shared with family or friends and need to switch to your own subscription, you can transfer your profile to keep your watch history and settings intact instead of starting from scratch. You can initiate a profile transfer on a TV-connected device. Note that account holders have to approve transfer requests within seven days, and once expired, transfer requests cannot be resubmitted—so be sure to let the primary user know that you've made the request.

If you've shared your Hulu login information with friends or activated your account on devices you don't own, you may want to regularly audit where your account is being used and remove any that don't need access. This includes TVs in Airbnbs and hotels. If you stay logged in, unauthorized users may have access to your Hulu account and personal data. You can see activated devices (and their activation date) under Your Account > Watch Hulu on Your Devices > Manage Devices. Click Remove next to old or unrecognized devices.

Hulu has an offline mode that allows you to download shows and movies to watch when you don't have a network connection. This is useful for traveling or when you know your wifi or cell service will be limited. Downloads are only available on supported iOS and Android devices, which means you may have to consider how much space your content takes up. You can select High for video quality if you want maximum resolution, but you may want to choose Standard if you are short on storage. This option is available under Downloads > Settings > Video Quality on iOS and Account > Settings > Downloads > Video Quality on Android. Note that once you click play on downloaded content, you have 48 hours to watch it before it expires—so don't start it unless you are ready.

If you have a Hulu + Live TV subscription, you must designate a "Home" network, which determines the local channels included in your plan. You can update your location up to four times within a 12-month period, but this limitation is meant to prevent viewers outside a household from sharing a subscription. Hulu does allow you to stream live TV on mobile when you're away from your home network (within the U.S.) as long as you access your account on that network every 30 days. If you travel often, check in with your mobile device frequently to avoid being locked out when you're away. Note that you can still watch streaming content with no restrictions.

#3365. Dragon Ball’s Best Episode In 8 Years Proves Fans Were Wrong About The Series’ New Anime

The Dragon Ball Super: Beerus anime has been doing a great job of removing unnecessary filler and improving on the original Dragon Ball Super series, but changes in the latest episode were so good that they've justified the entire project. While long-time Dragon Ball fans have been anxiously awaiting the continuation of the story in the Galactic Patrol arc, the news that the latest anime project would be devoted to improving Dragon Ball Super's first three arcs felt like a waste of Toei's talents, but the latest episode proves those fears were unfounded.

When the original Dragon Ball Super anime first aired, its extremely rushed and poorly planned production cycle created episodes that were lacking in many ways. With the franchise being one of the world's most beloved, the anime's static battles and mind-numbing filler material deflated the years of hype that had been building for Dragon Ball's anime return.

In 2015, episode #5 of Dragon Ball Super featured Goku's first sparring match against Beerus, the God of Destruction. The battle's flat presentation and underwhelming choreography felt like a mistake that nearly destroyed the hype the Dragon Ball franchise had built for its return. The goal of Dragon Ball Super: Beerus was to fix those mistakes and also make the Destroyer God more intimidating, and after six episodes, it's clear that goal has been accomplished.

It didn't take long for Dragon Ball Super: Beerus to prove that it would be different from the original anime and even the Battle of Gods movie. The first arc of the franchise's big revival introduced the God of Destruction, Beerus, and his Angel attendant Whis. It was an arc that took the first anime series 14 episodes to tell, but the new series was able to condense that all into only six episodes, with the sixth episode being the perfect example of the series' improvements.

Now that the production team was given time and the opportunity to revise previously released content, far more detail, upgraded coloring, and even entirely new animations help fix the series' stalest moments. Those improvements can be noticed in several of episode #6's upgraded scenes. This is especially true during Goku's first battle as a Super Saiyan God, which now includes higher levels of drama and intensity, especially with the changes to Beerus.

After watching from the sidelines for weeks, English dub viewers finally have an official streaming schedule for Dragon Ball Super.

One particular part had Beerus holding Goku underwater, and in the original series, the Saiyan broke out of the hold, violently pushing the God of Destruction back while Beerus made a silly expression of surprise. It was one of the many moments with the Destroyer that was played for comedy. However, the new Dragon Ball anime has removed a lot of those moments, with episode six even replacing Beerus's expression with one of competent curiosity, one that reminds viewers that Beerus was always in control.

Besides the improved artwork, pacing, and music, brand-new sequences have also helped Dragon Ball Super: Beerus feel more than a simple remaster cash grab. Near the end of Goku and Beerus's match at the highest levels of Earth's atmosphere, an added monologue from the Destroyer God to an unconscious Goku saw Beerus explicitly express his respect for the Saiyan. It was an extremely rare peek into an important character's honest thoughts, and it was a moment that added to Beerus's developing humility and Goku's accomplishment of impressing him.

When it was announced that Dragon Ball Super: Beerus would be condensing the original series' first 41 episodes into only 19, it was inevitable that some good material would land on the cutting room floor. Fortunately, the remastered series removed most of the scenes that failed to move the main plot forward, including the Pilaf gang's annoying side-quest to steal the Dragon Balls. Still, there were a few moments that were drastically shortened and some that were completely removed that I wish had stayed.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has premiered on Crunchyroll, and the first episode of the anime is so popular that it crashed the streaming service.

Moments that were specifically missing from the part of the story that episode #6 covered were great character moments for Piccolo, Whis, and even Goku. The part where Piccolo grabs Whis's arm, and the Angel's demeanor suddenly shifts into a cold and threatening tone, is gone. Notably, a fan-favorite moment where Goku breaks through several layers of Earth's bedrock while screaming "I won't let you destroy my world!" at the God of Destruction also did not make it into Dragon Ball Super: Beerus. Those scenes add moments of hype and character depth that new audiences will miss if this is all they watch.

One of the most divisive alterations relates to Vegeta', and the depths he was willing to go to protect the new life he's worked so hard to create. In both the Battle of Gods movie and the original Dragon Ball Super anime, Vegeta is willing to embarrass himself in an attempt to entertain Beerus. It showed that the safety of his family now means more to him than his Saiyan pride. That change removed a moment that speaks to Vegeta's character development and ultimately helped improve the overall narrative.

Now that the first Dragon Ball Super arc has concluded in the remastered series, it's safe to say that it's an improvement. Large sections of the original series that focused on unfunny and uninteresting scenes involving characters who have no narrative impact on future events severely dragged the pacing. And when battles did finally happen, the flat animation and repeated sequences felt like another insult that ultimately repelled viewers who'd grown up idolizing Dragon Ball Z. Thankfully, Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has addressed those glaring problems and become the best way to enjoy the beginning of the sequel series.

Even though Goku & Vegeta's strength has become godly, there are still a handful of Dragon Ball characters they can't & may never be able to defeat.

The first arc has been an improvement in almost every way, but there are still scenes that Toei left in that could have been removed. The shapeshifting pig, Oolong, hasn’t provided anything important to the narrative in decades, which is why it was baffling to see his prolonged game of rock-paper-scissors against Beerus remain in the new series. Still, even if a few moments like that stay and reduce the time for beloved scenes, Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has made enough smart and exciting changes to change my mind about it and power up my anticipation for more.

Apple first introduced the double-tap gesture control for Apple Watch back in 2023. Simply tap your index finger and thumb together twice on your watch-wearing wrist to execute actions like answering a call, closing an app, stopping a timer, or pausing a song.

In 2026, Apple added a single-tap gesture that works in exactly the same way, minus the second tap. To set it up, head to Settings > Gestures. Super-useful, I have my double-tap programmed to open the Smart Stack, while the single-tap opens my most recent/active widget, all without interacting with the screen or buttons.

When it comes to on-wrist safety, I'd argue that Apple and Google lead the pack, and one of my favorite Apple Watch personal safety features, Check In, often gets overlooked.

Check In is a reliable and simple way to keep friends and/or loved ones looped into your location at critical times. For example, I can set a Check In when I leave my apartment that automatically alerts my partner when I arrive at my set destination.

Or, if you're an avid runner, you can use the feature to automatically keep those you trust informed of when you both depart and arrive safely back home. Here's a deeper dive into how to use one of Apple's best safety features.

While on the subject of safety, I'd be remiss not to mention Apple's equally valuable Backtrack safety feature, which is particularly useful when exploring new places, if for nothing else, peace of mind.

Backtrack works like a digital breadcrumb trail, allowing you to retrace your steps back to your starting location via turn-by-turn directions in the event you get lost. Best of all, it works both in urban environments and out in nature.

Here's more on how to set up and use Apple's Backtrack tool.

Last but not least, and perhaps the easiest to miss, we have Apple's silent, vibration-based alarm clock. This is by no means a new feature, but it's one I adore and use daily.

As a U.S. West Coast-based writer with colleagues primarily in New York and London, my days tend to start quite early. Rather than risking waking my sleep partner or puppy, I schedule my alarm and set my Apple Watch 12 to silent. This switches the wake-up alert from an audible one to a vibration-based one, which I also find to be a gentler way to snap into reality.

What's your favorite lesser-known Apple Watch feature or app? Let me know in the comments below.

#3363. How to Make Sure an 'Onion' Site on the Dark Web Is Legitimate

Thankfully, Tor Browser already has a cryptography-backed feature that can verify the authenticity of an onion site, by confirming whether it has end-to-end encryption and extended validation certificates. Here's how this feature works, where it falters, as well as what other red flags you should look for.

While phishing on the dark web works as it does on the clear web, scammers have a few unique advantages due to the secretive nature of the environment. Most importantly, you can’t just glance at an onion link to tell if the site is genuine. Normal website URLs tend to be short and memorable, while onion links are 56-character strings of alphanumeric text that look mostly like gibberish.

When you try to connect, Tor Browser verifies the URL against the originating website’s cryptographic key, which is how you know nobody has hijacked the address or tampered with it midway. But since this has the unwanted effect of making domains harder to recall, scammers have a much easier time generating lookalike addresses or creating website clones.

For example, many popular websites use “vanity prefixes” to make their onion addresses more easily identifiable or to add some branding appeal. That means their 56-character onion link starts with something like “facebook,” “bbcnews,” or “ciadotgov.” But scammers can use a free tool like mkp224o to generate lookalike addresses with the same vanity prefix as the legitimate website, which gives users a false sense of security.

Of course, most dark web users don’t type addresses directly into Tor Browser; they use dark web directories like the Hidden Wiki to find useful onion sites relevant to their search. Scammers will create fake search engines or link directories to point users to their fake websites, like when the Ahmia search engine discovered that a copy of its platform was directing users to 255 cloned services back in 2015.

Of course, it’s possible to orchestrate phishing attempts that don’t involve cloning sites at all. Researchers at Freie Universität Berlin describe a sophisticated technique where attackers serve the real website through their own reverse proxy, which lets them manipulate parts of the site or log your online activity without your awareness. In 2019, ESET even found a trojanized version of Tor Browser that replaced Bitcoin addresses on websites to direct payments to hackers. So both genuine websites and your browser itself are also vulnerable to manipulation if you download or access them from an unverified source.

There are a few best practices to avoid phishing attacks when using the dark web. None of them are foolproof on their own, but together, they considerably lower the risk of ending up on a fake or manipulated website.

On the desktop version of Tor Browser, you can access an onion site using a shortened version of its URL called an Onion Name. For now, this feature only works with SecureDrop, so newsrooms can establish tip lines with addresses like mysitename.securedrop.tor.onion, which would then redirect to the 56-character original onion address. This feature is in active development, so more platforms might support it in the future.

When you load up an onion site using the Tor Browser, you’ll see an onion icon on the address bar, which confirms that your connection is end-to-end encrypted. But you can also click on the onion icon to check if the site has an Extended Validation (EV) certificate, which tells you that its authenticity has been verified by a trusted certificate authority like DigiCert. While not every legitimate onion site will have an EV certificate, famous ones like Facebook tend to.

On the other hand, if you see a caution sign next to the onion icon, that means the site is using a self-signed or expired certificate that isn’t guaranteed by a trusted authority. It may also imply that the site is being served over an insecure URL. This doesn’t definitely tell you it’s a phishing site, but it’s a red flag to watch out for nevertheless.

Don’t rely on search engines, link directories, Reddit threads, or Telegram channels too heavily on the dark web. Once you’re sure you’ve found the onion address for a genuine site, bookmark it so you can access it directly the next time you want to visit.

If you realized that you’ve been the victim of a phishing attempt, the first step is to close the browser window with the fake site and access the real onion address to reset any account passwords you may have accidentally divulged.

Also, generally try to enable two-factor authentication and PGP logins on any dark web account that supports it for added security. And if you downloaded Tor Browser from anywhere other than the official Tor Project site, uninstall it now and grab a fresh copy from the official address.

#3362. Elden Ring: Become Lord Officially Releases January 2027

Elden Ring will be nearing its fifth anniversary next January, and it's become increasingly clear in the time since release that the game won't be going away any time soon. The open-world Soulslike has proven to be one of the defining games of its generation, and its longevity has been helped along by the release of the massive Shadow of the Erdtree expansion and the standalone multiplayer title Elden Ring Nightreign.

It doesn't look like another game is set to arrive any time soon — developer FromSoftware has The Duskbloods up next instead — but that doesn't mean that Elden Ring will be leaving the spotlight. Elden Ring: Become Lord takes a new look at the Shardbearers in a manga format, and the English translation of its first volume is almost here.

Per the official Yen Press website, Elden Ring: Become Lord, Vol. 1 will release on January 26, 2027, in both paperback and digital formats. As a paperback volume, the manga will retail for $20.00, while the digital version will slash the price to $9.99. Along with direct pre-orders from the Yen Store, the volume is also available for pre-order from major booksellers like Amazon, Barnes & Noble, Books-A-Million, and Kinokuniya.

Like the game, Elden Ring: Become Lord follows a Tarnished protagonist, using the character as a tool to chronicle the stories of various Shardbearers. In true FromSoft fashion, the official description promises that "the path ahead is perilous indeed, for the shardbearers will not relinquish their power without a fight." The manga art comes from Tegekiken, with the script credited to 21g and original story to FromSoftware via the game.

If you're wondering why there's such a price discrepancy between digital and physical versions of Elden Ring: Become Lord, Vol. 1, it's presumably due to the format. Unlike the typical black-and-white approach for most manga, Become Lord advertises itself as a "beautiful full-color retelling," inherently driving up the production cost of a physical copy, and it features a larger trim size of 7"x10" that's more comparable to trade paperbacks for western comics than to typical manga publication. It's a fairly standard length, however, with a listed count of 176 pages.

This isn't the first Elden Ring manga to be published, but it should offer a very different experience from its predecessor. Yen Press also released Elden Ring: The Road to the Erdtree, a comedic, gag-focused retelling of the game. Nine volumes of The Road to the Erdtree are currently available in English, with the tenth set to arrive on February 23, 2027, one day before Elden Ring's fifth anniversary. There's also Elden Ring: Distant Tales Between, which focuses on the side stories of various characters.

If you're curious to find out more about Elden Ring: Become Lord, the contents of the first volume have been officially available in Japanese for a while, so there are already plenty of opinions out there. If you'd rather just go in relatively blind for another Elden Ring adventure, thoguh, the remaining wait won't be too long now.

I'm so happy. It could have been unofficially released after all.

#3361. The 8 Heaviest Family Movies, Ranked

There's an assumption that family movies are meant to be the safe option, whether that be from its colorful worlds, lovable characters, or stories that leave you feeling warm and fuzzy. But that's not always the case, as some of the films we grew up watching were considerably heavier than we might remember.

From devastating losses and childhood trauma to religious persecution, and the threat of nuclear destruction, these movies tackle some surprisingly bleak subject matter without softening its blow. Sure, they might be made appropriate for younger audiences, but that doesn't mean they're afraid to break (and horrify) a few hearts along the way. To buckle up because this is going to be a heavy watch.

Under the watchful eye of his mother (Paula Winslowe), Bambi begins to explore the world around him, until his idyllic childhood is quickly shattered by the actions of a hunter. Now growing older, Bambi (Donnie Dunagan) must learn to navigate the dangers of the wilderness, while also learning about friendship, love, and the realities of life—alongside his companions Thumper (Peter Behn) and Flower (Stan Alexander).

For a film often remembered as a sweet childhood classic, Bambi doesn't pull its punches when it comes to loss. The death of Bambi's mother remains one of Disney's most heartbreaking moments, made all the more devastating by how suddenly it happens and how little the young deer understands. It's also a surprisingly mature and profound story about growing up, with the changing seasons reflecting the joys and hardships that come with each stage of life.

In Don Bluth's animated fantasy, Mrs Brisby (Elizabeth Hartman) is a widowed field mouse facing an impossible dilemma: her family must leave their home before the farmer plows the field, but her youngest son, Timothy (Ina Fried), is too sick to make the journey. Desperate to save him, she seeks help from a group of highly intelligent rats living beneath a rose bush.

There's a surprising amount of darkness packed into The Secret of NIMH, from its eerie atmosphere and unsettling imagery to its exploration of grief, sacrifice, and mortality. Mrs Brisby's determination to save her family gives the story its emotional heart, but the film never pretends that doing the right thing comes without risk. Its willingness to tackle genuinely frightening ideas makes it a far more intense watch than its talking-animal premise might suggest—proving that you don't have to underestimate what younger audiences can handle.

Set during the summer of 1972, 11-year-old Vada Sultenfuss (Anna Chlumsky) is a precocious hyperhondriac girl growing up in a funeral home run by her widowed father. Her closest companion is Thomas J. Sennett (Macaulay Culkin), an equally awkward boy who shares her curiosity about the world. But as Vada navigates her first crushes, family changes, and the tribulations of growing up, she's forced to confront a loss far more devastating than anything she could've imagined.

My Girl is a deceptively gentle coming-of-age story that builds such a warm connection between its young characters that its emotional gut punch feels almost unfair. Chlumsky and Culkin are wonderfully natural together, capturing the innocence and intensity of a childhood friendship. But it's the film's treatment of grief that's particularly affecting because it doesn't offer easy explanations or try to make tragedy feel meaningful. Instead, it shows the messiness of a young person beginning to process something well beyond their years.

Based on Louis Sacher's bestselling novel, Stanley Yelnats (Shia LaBeouf), a teenager who's wrongly convicted of stealing a pair of shoes, is sent to Camp Green Lake, a juvenile detention facility in the middle of the desert. There, he and the other boys are forced to dig enormous holes everyday under the watch of the intimidating Warden (Sigourney Weaver). The official explanation is that the digging builds character, but as Stanley uncovers the camp's secrets, he also begins to unravel a family curse stretching back generations.

For all its quirky humor and mystery-solving, Holes has a surprisingly bleak view of justice as its characters are dealing with abandonment, prejudice, and the consequences of choices made long before they were born. Luckily, Stanley's friendship with Zero (Khleo Thomas) gives the film its emotional center, particularly as the pair find solidarity in a place designed to break them down. Consider this a clever, satisfying adventure, but one that also understands how much a little kindness and loyalty can matter in an unfair world.

Quasimodo (Tom Hulce) is a young man who has spent his entire life hidden away in the bell tower of Paris' Notre Dame Cathedral. Raised by the treacherous Judge Claude Frollo (Tony Jay), who convinces him that the outside world will reject him because of his appearance, Quasimodo longs to experience life beyond the cathedral walls. Thankfully, the Festival of Fools takes place, where he finally ventures into the city and befriends Esmerelda (Demi Moore), a Romani dancer whose compassion challenges everything he's been taught about the world and those within it.

As one of Disney's darkest films, The Hunchback of Notre Dame tackles prejudice, religious hypocrisy, persecution, and the abuse of power with a seriousness that still sets it apart from the studio's other family classics. All of this stems from the chilling villain Frollo, whose treatment of Quasimodo remains a sustained exercise in emotional abuse, while his persecution of the Romani people escalates into imprisonment, torture, and genocide. Even its final show-stopping number becomes an unsettling exploration of lust and self-righteous cruelty, making the film's dark themes hard to miss.

Set in 1950s America at the height of Cold War paranoia, young Hogarth Hughes (Eli Marienthal) discovers a gigantic robot that has crash-landed near his small town. And despite its enormous size and mysterious origins, the Giant (Vin Diesel) is gentle and curious, leading the two to quickly form an unlikely friendship. But when a government agent becomes convinced the machine is a threat to national security, Hogarth must find a way to protect his new friend before fear and suspicion turn into something much more dangerous.

Beneath its charming adventure lies a surprisingly moving story about identity, empathy, and the choice between destruction and compassion. Sure, The Giant may have been built as a weapon, but Hogarth teaches him that he doesn't have to be defined by what he was made to do. That message gives the film a powerful emotional core, particularly as the threat of nuclear war hangs over the story. Its final moments are among the most affecting in animated cinema, proving that even a giant robot can deliver one of the most human tales about sacrifice and love.

DreamWorks' epic animated musical retells the biblical story of Moses (Val Kilmer), who is raised as an Egyptian prince alongside his brother Rameses (Ralph Fiennes), both unaware of his true heritage. But when he discovers the truth about his birth and the suffering of his people under Egyptian rule, Moses leaves the palace and eventually returns with a divine mission: to convince Rameses to free the enslaved.

For a so-called family film, The Prince of Egypt doesn't soften the brutality of the story it tells. For one, its opening depicts soldiers tearing infants from their mothers and throwing them into the Nile, while the eventual plagues bring increasingly devastating consequences, including the deaths of Egypt's firstborn children. The spectacle is truly impressive, but the film's real weight comes from the personal cost of the conflict, particularly the painful divide between Moses and Rameses. There's no doubt that this is an ambitious family film that takes the themes of faith and suffering very seriously.

Based on Katherine Paterson's classic novel, Jess Aarons (Josh Hutcherson) is a lonely young boy who struggles to fit in at school and feels overlooked at home. But his life changes when he befriends Leslie Burke (AnnaSophia Robb), a new girl with a vivid imagination and a knack for seeing magic in the ordinary. Together, they create an imaginary kingdom called Terabithia, where they can escape their everyday troubles and become the heroes of their own adventure. Sadly, their friendship is put to the ultimate test when tragedy strikes.

What makes Bridge to Terabithia so heartbreaking is the way it captures the intensity of childhood friendship before suddenly confronting its audience with a devastating loss. What can we say? The film's reputation for making audiences cry is well-earned as it beautifully showcases grief from a child's perspective. By allowing Jess to struggle with guilt and anger, the story doesn't offer an easy way out. As a result, Terabithia becomes more than an imaginary escape—it's a way for Jess to hold onto his friend and carry something of her with him. What a devastating reminder that childhood doesn't always protect you from utter heartbreak.

Building an interactive website for my family's monthly budget took less than 5 minutes

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Google's latest AI model might be one of its most useful yet, especially if you've ever wished you could create your own app without knowing how to code.

The model is designed to be faster and more efficient at everyday tasks, including coding, research, analyzing documents and building interactive websites. Unlike Gemini 4 Carbon, which focuses on more demanding reasoning tasks, Hydrogen prioritizes getting things done quickly without sacrificing too much intelligence.

But what caught my attention was Google's claim that Hydrogen can build more functional, feature-complete websites in fewer prompts.

I immediately thought about our family budget. Between groceries, recurring bills, subscriptions and the everyday purchases that add up faster than expected, I wanted something that would show where our money was going without requiring me to build a complicated spreadsheet.

Better yet, I wanted something I could share with my husband so we could look at the numbers together. Note: for this experiment, these numbers are arbitrary. Which reminds me, be sure your app is secure before sharing financial information.

Here's the exact prompt I used to create a budget for my family:

Build me a fully functional, interactive website that helps me figure out where my money goes every month.

Sign up to the Tom's AI Guide weekly newsletter summing up all the biggest AI news you need to know. Plus, analysis from our AI editors and tips on how to use the latest AI tools!

I want to enter my monthly income, recurring bills, groceries, subscriptions and miscellaneous expenses.

The website should automatically calculate how much money I have left, show an interactive breakdown of my spending, identify my three biggest opportunities to save money and let me simulate what happens if I cancel subscriptions or reduce spending.

Make it beautiful, modern, mobile-friendly and simple enough for someone who doesn't understand budgeting.

Use realistic sample data so I can test it immediately. Make every button, slider and calculation functional, not just decorative.

Do not ask follow-up questions. Make reasonable design decisions yourself and build the complete experience.

Before finishing, check the calculations, test the interactions and correct any problems you find. Tell me if anything could not be verified.

What makes this prompt interesting is that there are several things happening at once. Gemini needs to create the website, build the calculations, organize the information in a way that makes sense and connect everything so the numbers update when you change your spending. The key is the interactivity of the site. For example, canceling a $15 subscription should immediately increase the amount of money you have left by $15. Reducing your grocery budget should change your spending breakdown, and the savings recommendations should reflect the expenses you've entered.

It's exactly the kind of interactive web development that Google says Hydrogen is particularly good at. And best of all, you don't have to be "coder" to make it work for you.

The prompt also gives Gemini some creative freedom. You can certainly tell the model what colors you want, but I kept the prompt short for the sake of function. I didn't specify colors, layouts or exactly where every button should go because I just wanted to see my money/budget all in one place. You can do that, but you don't have to because the model make those design decisions on its own so you can focus on other things.

Head to Gemini and select Gemini 4 Hydrogen from the model options. It was the default for me, but if not, just select it from the model picker. It's free for everyone. If you don't see it, try logging out and refreshing. Google says Hydrogen is rolling out to users globally, although free accounts may access it through automatic model selection rather than a dedicated model choice.

Paste the prompt into the chat and ask Gemini to generate the website. Once it provides a working preview or code, explore the experience before adding your own numbers.

Start by changing the monthly income, removing a subscription and adjusting the grocery budget. Check whether the totals update correctly and whether any savings recommendations actually match the spending categories.

You should also test the website on your phone, since the prompt specifically requests a mobile-friendly design.

One important thing to remember is that generating a website and publishing one are different steps. If you want to share your budgeting app with your spouse, you'll need to use an available sharing or publishing option, or host the generated files yourself.

I'm already a fan of Gemini Hydrogen. It has proven to be a useful model in so many ways, particularly when I want questions answered quickly and intelligently.

A budgeting website is a good example because it's personal, practical and easy to evaluate. You don't need programming experience to know whether the numbers add up, whether the buttons work or whether the finished app makes managing your money easier.

And the same approach could work for a meal planner, family chore tracker, vacation budget or personalized fitness dashboard. Give it a try and let me know your thoughts about this model in the comments.

#3358. 4 Years After The Series' End, Disney's Amphibia Returns With Strange Voyage

Disney’s Amphibia is returning more than four years after its animated finale, although not with a new season. Creator Matt Braly is bringing the story back through Amphibia: Strange Voyage, a serialized comic published by TOKYOPOP and Disney Manga. Its first installment is scheduled to reach comic shops on January 13, 2027.

The announcement gives fans a reason to revisit Wartwood and the Plantars, while also setting up an adventure that moves beyond the television series’ final battle. Amphibia ran for three seasons on Disney Channel and ended on May 14, 2022, with “The Hardest Thing.” Strange Voyage picks up after that conclusion rather than retelling Anne Boonchuy’s original arrival.

The opening premise begins months after Anne saves Amphibia from the Core and returns to Earth. With that crisis behind them, the Plantars embark on a voyage to find a new continent. Their expedition does not go according to plan: a dangerous turn leaves the crew stranded on an unfamiliar island, where unexpected secrets await.

That setup gives the comic room to explore a part of Amphibia that the television series did not have time to map out. The animated show balanced its fantasy setting with comedy, friendship, and a coming-of-age story, but Strange Voyage introduces new territory and a fresh mystery. The island may prove as important as the destination.

Matt Braly is writing the new series, keeping its storytelling in the hands of the person who created Amphibia and guided its three-season run. Beatrice Bovo is providing the artwork, including the cover designs. Their collaboration gives the project a direct creative link to the original series while allowing a different artist to interpret its familiar characters.

Fans should not expect a handful of disconnected comic strips. Braly has described Strange Voyage as one continuous narrative planned across ten issues, with a new installment arriving every three weeks. He has also characterized it as an important canon miniseries, showing that the journey is intended to matter to the larger Amphibia story.

That distinction is worth paying attention to, especially for viewers who want the comic to build on the series rather than simply recreate its episodic humor. A serialized format gives the writers space to develop the island’s mysteries, the Plantars’ expedition and the consequences of the choices made along the way. The first three issues establish the opening stretch.

The release schedule starts with Amphibia: Strange Voyage #1 on January 13, 2027. Issue #2 is scheduled for February 3, followed by Issue #3 on February 24. Each issue is listed at $4.99, and the first three installments are 32 pages apiece, giving readers a regular way to follow the story.

Readers who would rather sample the comic series for free will have another opportunity in the spring. Amphibia: Strange Voyage – Issue #1 is among the titles announced for Comics Giveaway Day 2027, Penguin Random House’s branding for the 2027 Free Comic Book Day event. Participating comic shops are scheduled to hand out the giveaway books on Saturday, May 1.

There is an important distinction between that promotion and the regular release schedule: the listed giveaway is Issue #1, not a free collection of the first three installments. The January and February issues are separate $4.99 releases, so readers who want to keep up with the story before May will need to pick them up individually.

Atlantis: The Lost Empire is the most underrated movie in all of Disney, but 25 years later, it's finally getting the epic sequel it deserves.

Comics Giveaway Day could also introduce the series to readers who missed Amphibia during its Disney Channel run. The 2027 lineup includes books from several publishers, making the event a broad entry point for comic newcomers. For returning viewers, the bigger attraction is Braly’s continuation of the Plantars’ story in a planned canon adventure.

Black Friday is still a couple of weeks away, with the big shopping event falling on November 27, but Amazon's early Black Friday sale is already bringing some worthwhile discounts on Soundcore's Nebula projectors. Prices start at $299 for the compact Nebula P1i and go up to $2,799 for the premium X1S 4K laser projector, with savings of up to $700 across the models we've rounded up. There's quite a bit of variety here, too, from battery-powered projectors you can take camping or move between rooms to more powerful 4K models designed for a dedicated movie-night setup.

The Soundcore Nebula P1i is down to $299 from $399, while the Nebula P1 is $699.99, down from $799. Both offer 1080p resolution and Google TV, but their speaker setups are what make them interesting. The P1i has two 10W speakers that flip out and rotate to direct sound toward your seating area, while the P1's speakers detach completely and can run wirelessly for up to 20 hours. The P1 is also brighter at 650 ANSI lumens versus the P1i's 380, though you'll need a power outlet for either projector since neither has a built-in battery.

Small enough to slip into a bag, the Nebula Capsule 3 and Capsule 3 Laser are worth considering if you want something you can easily take on trips or move around the house. The standard Capsule 3 is down to $399 from $529, saving you $130, while the Laser version is $649.99, down from $749.99. Both offer 1080p resolution, automatic image adjustments, and up to 2.5 hours of battery life, although the Laser model is a little brighter at 300 ANSI lumens compared with the standard model's 200.

Taking movie night outdoors is a little easier with a battery-powered projector, and both the Nebula Mars 3 Air and Mars 3 are designed for just that. The smaller Mars 3 Air is down to $519.99 from $599.99, offering 1080p resolution, 400 ANSI lumens of brightness, and up to 2.5 hours of playback. The larger Mars 3, now $899.99 from $999.99, steps things up with 1,000 ANSI lumens, up to five hours of battery life in Eco mode, and a more powerful 40W speaker. It also has a weather-resistant design that's useful for camping or backyard screenings, though its extra bulk might make it less convenient to carry around.

If you're ready to move beyond 1080p, the Nebula Cosmos 4K SE at $1,099.99 (originally $1,299.99) offers a more affordable way to get 4K resolution. Its hybrid LED and laser light source delivers up to 1,800 ANSI lumens, while its Dolby Vision support helps bring out more detail in compatible movies and shows. You also get Google TV and automatic image adjustments for easier setup, though it doesn't have a built-in battery, so you'll need a power outlet nearby.

At the premium end of Nebula's lineup, the X1 and newer X1S are designed for a more serious home theater setup. The X1 is down to $2,299 from $2,999, saving you $700, while the X1S is $2,799 from $3,299. Both use triple-laser technology with 4K resolution, Dolby Vision, and optical zoom, but the X1S has a considerable advantage in brightness, reaching up to 6,000 ANSI lumens compared with the X1's 3,500. That extra brightness is useful in rooms with some ambient light, but the tradeoff is louder fan noise.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

The best thing you can do is compare the prices with other retailers that have Black Friday sales. If that seems like too much work, you can just follow our Black Friday coverage (we're already doing all the searching and vetting for you). Some other tips are making sure you're not being sold an older or cheaper version and always reading reviews.

#3356. ‘Supernatural’ Star Officially Lands in Netflix’s Next Mega Hit

Hannah covers horror, sci-fi, and games at Collider, where she writes news and features, reviews new releases, and interviews the people who make them. She’s helping build out Collider’s gaming coverage, with Pokémon as one of her specialties. If she isn’t writing about a monster, she’s probably watching one on a tape from her VHS collection.

One of the perks of being married to Jared Padalecki is that when your book club finds a romance you’d like to see him star in, you can take it up with him at home. In 2022, Genevieve Padalecki, who played Ruby opposite her future husband on Supernatural, picked up a book by fellow Texan Katherine Center. Four years later, the movie adaptation starring Padalecki is just hours from premiering on Netflix.

It’s easy to see what she had in mind for him. Between fifteen seasons of saving people as Sam Winchester and four more carrying a Texas Ranger’s badge on Walker, Padalecki looks like a pretty safe bet to get somebody home in one piece. This time, however, he plays the other half of that dynamic, and the person qualified to keep him alive is Leighton Meester.

Padalecki and Meester star in Guarding Stars, which premieres Wednesday, November 18, on Netflix. Based on Center’s 2022 novel The Bodyguard, the holiday rom-com follows action star Jack Stapleton (Padalecki), who has picked up a stalker just in time for Christmas at his family’s ranch. Bringing a bodyguard home would mean telling his family why he needs one, but bringing home a girlfriend buys him a perfectly good excuse to keep Hannah Brooks (Meester) close, provided nobody asks the happy couple too many questions.

Four love stories, four completely different ideas of what it means to be somebody's person. This is the one that matches how you actually fall, and what it would ask of you.

You do not fall for strangers. You fall for the person you have already been talking to for years, which is the slowest and by some distance the most durable way anybody has found to do this.

You want a partner, not an audience. Somebody who wants their own life as badly as you want yours, and who would never ask you to be smaller to make the relationship easier.

The intensity was never the problem. The secrecy is. You are drawn to a love that lives entirely in private, and to the particular ache of wanting somebody you are not supposed to want.

You do not do this cautiously. When it happens for you it is immediate and total and it rearranges everything, and you would not accept a smaller version of it.

Jack makes the mistake of questioning whether Hannah can protect him while they’re both still standing on the airport tarmac. By the time she’s finished answering, only one of them is still standing. Director Elizabeth Allen Rosenbaum told Swooon she hadn’t read Katherine Center’s book when the screenplay came her way, but she knew she wanted the job the moment Hannah tossed Jack over her shoulder. “I mean, how often does the romantic heroine get to throw her leading man over her shoulder? I was in.” Rosenbaum had directed Meester on Gossip Girl, where Blair Waldorf could do considerable damage to a man without having to lay a hand on him. For Guarding Stars, Meester learned how to flip a stunt performer, ride a horse, and jump clear of an explosion.

Padalecki, meanwhile, gets to put a considerably less lethal skill to use: he sings with country artist Walker Hayes on a Christmas parade float. Hayes originally auditioned to play Jack’s older brother, and when the filmmakers decided to make the brother younger, Rosenbaum rewrote the part of the town sheriff to keep him in the cast. Giving the sheriff a duet with Padalecki was also her idea.

Guarding Stars premieres November 18 on Netflix.

#3355. Jeff Bezos' Role In Robert Pattinson James Bond Casting Revealed

Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos reveals what role he had in casting Robert Pattinson as James Bond.

After acquiring half of the franchise and its distribution rights when it bought MGM, Amazon coaxed complete creative control of the James Bond franchise from longtime producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson. For the next film, Amazon hired Denis Villeneuve as director, with Stephen Knight writing the script, and after a long and exhaustive search, Robert Pattinson beat out several other candidates as James Bond.

Now, at Semafor's Silicon Valley & The World conference (via The Hollywood Reporter), Jeff Bezos says he was "heavily involved" in casting Pattinson as Bond, collaborating with Amazon MGM executives, producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman, and Villeneuve:

We ran a really tight process, and we made the final decision on Friday. There were a big group initially, and we selected down to five finalists, and then we did real old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists.

The shortlist is no secret at this point – Callum Turner, Josh O'Connor, Jack Lowden, Nicholas Hoult and, ultimately, Pattinson, who landed the coveted role. Bezos says the team conducted extensive screen tests, having each actor perform three scenes in full costume on constructed sets. They initially had reservations about Pattinson before coming around to the idea that he was the right fit:

They were all amazing, but there was something special about Rob and his performances, and it was kind of immediately un-debated. Denis, the director was, we all sort of gravitated to him. By the way, initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him just because he’s already so famous. We sort of thought, maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown. But in the screening tests, it was so obvious: He is James Bond.

Robert Pattinson's casting marks Amazon's most significant move yet since its acquisition of MGM and its subsequent buyout of the Broccoli family's stake, giving the company control of the franchise.

There's a certain irony in the shift, given that the James Bond movies have long featured tech billionaires and media moguls as villains, from Hugo Drax (Michael Lonsdale) in Moonraker (1979), Max Zorin (Christopher Walken) in A View to a Kill (1985), and Elliot Carver (Jonathan Pryce) in Tomorrow Never Dies (1997).

Now, the James Bond franchise is in the hands of one of the world's wealthiest men – whose business empire stretches across technology, media, entertainment, and even space exploration. And this time, the mogul is on the other side of the table, helping make the decisions.

Since Bezos was "heavily involved" in selecting the new 007, it stands to reason he will continue to be involved in casting the next Bond villain, too. In turn, it's unlikely the next Bond film will continue the tradition of tech billionaires as villains, since the Amazon CEO likely won't want to risk lampooning or villainizing himself. For now, it looks like the biggest Bond villain might be Bezos himself.

#3354. Apple HomeView launches tomorrow, but its first security update is already here

While the first HomeView units won’t reach customers until tomorrow, Apple today released a software update addressing nine security vulnerabilities. Here are the details.

Apple today released HomeView Software Version 27.2 (build 24V526), which contains some of the security fixes the company included in recent updates to its other operating systems, including iOS 27.2, macOS 27.2 Golden Gate, and iPadOS 27.2.

These include a vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to join an iMessage group chat and receive its messages, as well as another that could allow a malicious Bluetooth device to pair without user interaction.

In practice, this means that users who get the device starting tomorrow are advised to update it as soon as possible, since the vulnerabilities have been publicly disclosed.

Here’s the full security content of HomeView Software Version 27.2

Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to bypass the rate limit on pairing code attempts

Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management.

Impact: An app may be able to access sensitive user data

Description: An authorization issue was addressed with improved state management.

Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to corrupt process memory

Description: A use-after-free issue was addressed with improved memory management.

Impact: Processing maliciously crafted input may lead to memory corruption

Description: An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved input validation.

Impact: A malicious Bluetooth device may be able to establish a pairing without user interaction

Description: This issue was addressed with improved checks.

Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to bypass the rate limit on pairing code attempts and pair with a device without user interaction

Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management.

Impact: A remote attacker may be able to join an iMessage group chat and receive its messages

Description: An authorization issue was addressed with improved validation.

Impact: A user added to an iMessage group may be able to access messages sent before they joined

Description: This issue was addressed by removing the vulnerable code.

Impact: An attacker on the same network may be able to bypass the rate limit on AirPlay pairing code attempts

Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management.

Earlier today, Apple also confirmed that a software update coming next month will add support for security accessories to HomeView’s Siri AI, which currently refuses to unlock doors or open garage doors via voice commands.

Be sure to catch 9to5Mac’s full review of Apple HomeView ahead of tomorrow’s launch.
